# Heirloom public site: design and build brief

Build exactly this. It is the result of a research pass over about 90 reference sites. Where this brief and your taste disagree, follow the brief. Where it is silent, follow the rulebook at the end.

## 1. Job of the page
A visitor (a security engineer, a distro maintainer, an AI-agent builder) should understand in about 60 seconds that Heirloom did real work on its own and that they can verify any claim. **Sell proof, not patches.**
- Every competitor in end-of-life support (HeroDevs, TuxCare, Seal, Aikido, Chainguard) *claims* to patch. None publishes per-CVE proof of affected or not affected.
- Heirloom publishes a calibrated verdict per CVE × release line, receipts for each, and says what it could NOT prove.

## 2. Direction: "Conservation treatment record"
Django 4.2 is the *object*, and Heirloom is the conservator. The page reads like a museum conservation report crossed with an independent verification report (Jepsen analyses, The Markup's "Show your work").
- **Accession numbers:** each CVE is an entry `HL–4.2–001` … `HL–4.2–019`, ordered by advisory date then CVE id. Use en-dashes, set in mono.
- **Record fields:** Condition (the verdict per line) · Examination (calibration + gates) · Treatment (the PR, or the evidence issue) · Evidence (provenance, links).
- **The human question** is called "The conservator's query".
- **Figures are captioned** "Fig. 1 — The register", "Fig. 2 — …". Tables are "Table 2 — Backtest".

### Colour (CSS custom properties; light is canonical)
- **Page:** `--paper #F7F7F4`, `--ink #17181A`, `--muted #66645E`, `--rule #DAD9D3`, `--surface #FFFFFF` (sheet).
- **The register sheet only** (Fig. 1 is the only "paper" object on the page; real bookkeeping ledger paper):
  - `--ledger #EEF2EA`;
  - blue rules `--ledger-rule #C9D6E3`, aligned exactly to table row lines;
  - a double red margin rule `--margin #C8463D` at about 60% opacity, as two 1 px vertical lines after the accession column.
  - No other texture anywhere: no noise, no grain, no `feTurbulence`.
- **Verdict chips** (text on fill, 1 px border in the text colour at about 25%):

  | Chip | Text | Fill | Symbol |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | FIX READY | `#1F4720` | `#D8EFDF` | ✓ |
  | NOT AFFECTED | `#194168` | `#D3E3FC` | ○ |
  | UNPROVEN | `#7A4A00` | `#F6E6C4` | ? |
  | AFFECTED | `#9B1C1C` | `#FBE1D1` | ! |
  | NO PROBE | `#66645E` | `#ECEBE6` | – |

  Every chip shows its symbol AND its word. Colour is never the only cue. Verify AA contrast.
- **Dark mode** ("night reading room"): redefine every token under `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, plus a manual toggle (`data-theme`).
  - Values: paper `#121315`, ink `#ECEAE4`, muted `#A19E96`, rule `#2B2C2F`, ledger `#16201A`, ledger-rule `#24384A`, margin `#C8463D` at 50%.
  - Chips get dark fills with light same-hue text: e.g. FIX READY text `#BFE8CC` on `#173523`. Check AA for each.
- **Forbidden:** cream `#F4F1EA` with terracotta, purple, gradients on text, glows, glassmorphism.

### Type
- **Newsreader** (`@fontsource-variable/newsreader`, opsz axis) for display and text. **IBM Plex Mono** (`@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono`, 400/500) for data only: CVE ids, hashes, accession numbers, version strings, field labels, the meta line.
- Self-host, latin subset only, `font-display: swap`, preload the display font. Total ≤100 kB.
- Rules: display ≤ 6rem; tracking ≥ −0.03em; `text-wrap: balance` on headings and `pretty` on paragraphs; measure ≤ 72ch; `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on every number. No eyebrow labels above headings: field labels sit inline, in mono small caps.

### Seal mark
An SVG wax-seal monogram: a slightly irregular circle (8–12 soft lobes), a ring inside it, and a serif "H" (from Newsreader, converted to paths or drawn).
- One flat colour: `--margin` red in light mode, a lighter red in dark mode. No gradients.
- Used in the nav (24 px), the favicon (SVG plus a 32 px PNG), the OG card and the footer.
- No mascot or character.

### Motion (restrained; one orchestrated moment)
- **The single orchestrated moment is the campaign replay** (§3.3). Nothing else animates on scroll: no section fade-ups, no parallax, no scroll-jacking, no looping background effects.
- **Chip ink-in** (replay only): opacity 0→1 plus scale 0.96→1, 180 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)`, with a 30–60 ms stagger within a batch.
- **Sheet:** 280 ms, `cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)`; exit faster (200 ms).
- **Press feedback:** `scale(0.97)` on `:active`, 160 ms ease-out.
- **Hover:** only under `@media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`, and only colour or underline changes of ≤150 ms. Matrix cells don't animate on hover.
- **Reduced motion:** `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">`, plus a CSS fallback (`0.01ms` durations, `scroll-behavior:auto`). With reduced motion, the replay steps between states without transforms.
- Animate only `transform` and `opacity`. Never `transition: all`.

## 3. Page structure (single page `index.html`, plus `404.html`)
Use a 12-column grid with generous margins. Content is left-aligned at a report measure. The register may run full-bleed within the container. Sections are separated by fine rules and `* * *`, never coloured boxes or bento cards.

1. **Nav** (sticky, quiet):
   - seal + "Heirloom";
   - links: Register · Finding · Method · Query · Results · Verify;
   - right side: GitHub (repo) and the theme toggle;
   - on mobile it collapses to a sheet menu.
2. **Hero / abstract** (no hero image; the register is the visual):
   - **H1:** "Django stopped patching 4.2 on 7 April 2026. Debian 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 still ship it."
   - **Sub:** "Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched — and proves which old versions are actually vulnerable."
   - **Abstract** (one paragraph, every number from data): what it did with the 19 post-EOL advisories: N fix ready (candidate backport PRs, probe FAIL×3 → PASS×3), N proven not affected, N unproven with evidence filed, and 1 question asked whose answer it reused.
   - **Mono meta line:** `Record HL–4.2 · 19 advisories · 3 release lines · data generated <iso> · built during neatHack, Oct 10–12 2026`.
   - **CTAs:** "Open the register" (scrolls to Fig. 1) and "Read a backport" (PR #13). Text buttons, not pills.
3. **Fig. 1 — The register** (the hero data):
   - A real `<table>`:
     - columns: Accession / CVE + one-line title / Django 4.2.30 (upstream) / Debian 13 · 4.2.28 / Ubuntu 24.04 · 4.2.11 + Ubuntu patches;
     - use the exact distro version strings available in the data;
     - a row total (e.g. "2 of 3 lines affected"), as in curl's vulnerability table;
     - a sticky first column;
     - `<th scope>` everywhere.
   - **Cells are buttons** that open the receipt. Arrow keys move between cells (roving tabindex, one tab stop); Enter/Space opens; Home/End go to the row start or end.
   - **Filter:** a ToggleGroup above the table with live counts per verdict (e.g. `FIX READY 13`), in the style of Oxide's RFD filters.
   - **Replay scrubber** above the table: the single orchestrated moment.
     - Dated stops: 2026-04-07 Django 4.2 end of life · 05-05 · 06-03 · 07-07 · 08-04 · 10-01 "Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 patch" · 10-06 · 10-09.
     - Rows ink in as their advisory batch arrives. A play button walks the stops over about 8 s. It's an `<input type="range">` underneath, so it works with the keyboard.
     - An `aria-live="polite"` line reads e.g. "Aug 4 2026 · 15 of 19 advisories".
     - At 10-06, draw a thin connector (an SVG path in the margin) from CVE-2026-87890's row to CVE-2026-15307's row, labelled "stacked on our own backport · PR #21 on #20".
     - Put a small "query #6" marker on 15307's row.
     - **Default state on load is the END (everything visible)**; the replay is opt-in ("Replay the campaign").
   - **Mobile (<768 px):** one card per CVE (accession, CVE, title, three line chips), with the same tap-to-open receipt.
   - **Caption:** "Fig. 1 — The register. Every cell is a test run you can open." Add a legend for the five chips.
4. **Receipt** (the shadcn Sheet; right on ≥768 px, bottom below; content lazy-loaded):
   - **Header:** accession, CVE id, title, advisory date, link to the advisory.
   - **Condition:** a chip per line.
   - **Examination:**
     - the calibration triangle as a small figure: U⁻ (upstream before fix) FAIL ×3 · U⁺ (upstream after fix) PASS ×3 · this line → result, with the failing test ids;
     - gates C0–C4 as a checklist with their detail strings;
     - probe origin ("written by the independent porter, <model>" or "hand-written").
   - **Treatment:** the PR link with "probe FAIL×3 → PASS×3", plus a note when it applied precedent P001 or is stacked on #20. Or the evidence issue link with its reason.
   - **Evidence:** run id, Entire checkpoint id, neatlogs trace id (copy buttons), $ cost and minutes, raw logs link, and the reproduce command `heirloom report --cve <id>`.
   - **Behaviour:** focus trap, Esc closes, focus returns to the cell, and the URL hash `#HL-4.2-007` deep-links to an open receipt.
5. **The finding — Fig. 2** (told on the page, no scroll-jacking): three dated steps side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile:
   - Oct 1: Ubuntu ships its CVE-2026-15307 patch for noble;
   - Oct 6: Django discloses CVE-2026-87890 (bytes in spatial lookups), an amendment to the 15307 fix;
   - our probe on noble's tree: FAIL ×3.
   - **Claim sentence, verbatim:** "noble's CVE-2026-15307 backport leaves the bytes path that upstream closed as CVE-2026-87890; our calibrated probe shows it."
   - Then: "The probe is hand-written and calibrated on Django's own fix commits (FAIL ×3 before dd0558d1, PASS ×3 after)."
   - Link the raw logs. No exploitability claim, no other Ubuntu release.
6. **Method — "How a verdict is earned"** (The Markup style). The rule in display type: "Never trust a test that hasn't failed." Then five numbered stages, each with one sentence and the artifact that proves it:
   - Locate the fix;
   - Write an independent probe (the porter never sees the fix's code hunks);
   - Calibrate on upstream before/after (FAIL×3 / PASS×3, coverage reaches the fix, mutants caught);
   - Adapt and verify on the old line (fail→pass, no new failures);
   - Decide and publish (PR with a claim table, or evidence; ask once when a choice is real).
7. **The conservator's query:** a vertical dated timeline from `campaign_evidence.json`:
   - question #6 opened by CVE-2026-15307 (asked_at);
   - CVE-2026-84429 waits instead of asking;
   - answered `adopt-upstream-tests`;
   - precedent P001 stored (stored_at);
   - #20 applies it; #19 reuses it without asking;
   - #21 stacked on #20.
   Each step links its issue, PR or trace id.
8. **Table 2 — Backtest** (from `evals/results.json`): v1 naive vs v2 Heirloom on cases with known answers. Show accuracy (decided), **false NOT AFFECTED (1 vs 0, emphasized)**, UNPROVEN and escalation. Add one sentence on why a false "not affected" is the dangerous error, and one on the neatlogs detection that flags it.
9. **Stated limits** (as in Jepsen's limits paragraph; honest, short, a list):
   - candidate backports, not Django releases;
   - tests run on SQLite and PostGIS only;
   - UNPROVEN by design for what it can't exercise;
   - the 87890 matrix probe is hand-written;
   - the recovery shown was a worker killed during a harness restart;
   - the campaign's harness was fixed and restarted 4× mid-run, and each restart resumed from the ledger with nothing published twice;
   - the porter sees the advisory and upstream's test diff, never the fix's code hunks.
10. **Economics (cfo.ai):** measured model cost per CVE and machine minutes per CVE (from data), with pricing hypotheses clearly labelled "hypothesis". Links to the three read-only cfo.ai Pages (Base / Bear / Bull) and to `docs/business-plan.md`.
11. **Verify it yourself**, as a "front shelf" list in the style of Dynamicland:
    - all PRs (number · CVE · one-line title · line · FAIL×3→PASS×3);
    - all evidence issues (number · CVE · reason);
    - Entire: build sessions are linked from commit trailers. Show the command `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)'`, plus the runtime checkpoints on every backport commit;
    - the neatlogs detections JSON;
    - endoflife.date/django as outside confirmation of the EOL date;
    - the repository.
12. **Footer / colophon:**
    - the seal;
    - "Heirloom — keeps end-of-life software patched";
    - fonts (Newsreader, IBM Plex Mono);
    - "Data generated <iso> from evals/*.json and the campaign ledger";
    - "Built with neatlogs · Entire · cfo.ai during neatHack";
    - MIT; repo link.

**404:** "This accession number is not in the register." Show a link back and the seal.

## 4. Data (no hand-typed numbers)
- First run `heirloom export --out site/data` (it refreshes the snapshot).
- `site/web/scripts/build-data.mjs` reads the files below and writes `site/web/public/site.json` (≤150 kB) plus `src/data/types.ts`. It fails the build loudly if a required field is missing.
  - `site/data/{campaign,matrix,backtest,events,index}.json`, `site/data/cve/*.json`, `site/data/line/*.json`;
  - `evals/campaign_evidence.json`, `evals/results.json`, `evals/results_live.json`, `evals/detections.json`;
  - the inputs table in `docs/business-plan.md`.
- **Scope:** the register shows the 19 post-EOL CVEs. Counts must equal the README first screen. Add a unit test (vitest) for that.
- **Links:** PR and issue URLs come from the data. A check script verifies each returns 200 via `gh api`.

## 5. Stack
- Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Tailwind CSS v3 with CSS-variable tokens.
- shadcn/ui (Radix): Sheet, Table, Tabs, ToggleGroup, Tooltip, Badge, Button.
- `motion` with `LazyMotion` + `m` + `domAnimation` (never the full `motion` component).
- Magic UI number-ticker only if patched for `useReducedMotion` and `tabular-nums`; otherwise plain numbers.
- Lucide icons.
- No anime.js, no Vaul, no Aceternity effects, no animated grids or beams.
- Code lives in `site/web/`. Base path `/heirloom/`.
- Deploy with `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (checkout → setup-node 22 → `npm ci` → build → upload-pages-artifact → deploy-pages). Enable it once with `gh api -X POST repos/iamdflame/heirloom/pages -f build_type=workflow`. The URL is https://iamdflame.github.io/heirloom/. **Deploy a skeleton first** so the URL is live early.
- **Meta:** title "Heirloom — keeps end-of-life software patched"; description; canonical URL; OG and Twitter `summary_large_image` with `og.png` (1200×630, rendered by Playwright from an `/og.html` view: seal, the headline, a miniature of the register's counts); SVG favicon.

## 6. QA loop (repeat until clean; ≥3 cycles across B7a and B7b)
- `scripts/qa.mjs` (Playwright + Chromium + `@axe-core/playwright`) against `vite preview`. For each run:
  - **Screenshots:** 390×844, 768×1024, 1440×900, 1920×1080; light and dark; `reducedMotion: 'reduce'` once; the replay at its start, middle and end; the receipt open on desktop and mobile. Save to `site/web/qa/<cycle>/`, which is git-ignored.
  - **Keyboard flow:** Tab into the register → ArrowRight / ArrowDown → Enter opens the receipt → Esc closes → focus is back on the same cell.
  - **axe:** zero serious or critical violations.
  - **Console:** zero errors or warnings.
  - **Lighthouse** with the Playwright Chromium (`npx lighthouse … --chrome-flags=--headless`): ≥95 for performance, accessibility, best practices and SEO on mobile.
  - **Budgets:** JS ≤150 kB gzip on first load, fonts ≤100 kB.
- **Read every screenshot PNG yourself** and write the concrete defects you see (alignment, spacing rhythm, wrapping, contrast, orphan words, overflow, chip clipping) into `site/web/PROGRESS.md` before fixing them. Never claim something was verified unless the script or your own look at the PNG did it.

## 7. Rulebook (from the research; apply everywhere)
1. Use only these 5 chip colours + the 5 page tokens. Never `bg-blue-500` and the like: use semantic tokens.
2. Radii: chips 4 px, sheet 12 px. Pick ONE elevation per component (a border or a shadow, not both).
3. Hit targets ≥44×44 on touch and ≥40×40 in dense desktop UI. Each matrix cell button fills its cell.
4. Focus: `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px }`. Never remove outlines.
5. Use `aria-live` for replay progress and the filter result count. Every state change needs a static cue too.
6. Tooltips only ever duplicate information; nothing essential lives only in a tooltip.
7. No emoji used as icons. No "→" appended to link text. No 01/02/03 numbering except the Method stages and the timeline.
8. Pick links to show from the data, never invent them. If a field is missing, hide the row; don't print "undefined".
9. Lazy-load the receipt sheet code. Load no images except the seal SVG and the OG PNG.
10. Copy is plain and specific. Never write "revolutionary", "seamless", "cutting-edge" or "AI-powered".

# Heirloom

**Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched.** For each new upstream security fix it writes an independent probe, calibrates it on upstream's own before/after commits, proves on the old line whether the bug is there, and then publishes either a verified candidate backport or the evidence of why it could not decide.

- **19 post-EOL Django CVEs on 4.2:** **13** AFFECTED · **1** NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN · **5** UNPROVEN ([results_live.json](evals/results_live.json)).
- **13 candidate backport PRs**, 13 of 13 with the probe FAIL ×3 before → PASS ×3 after the fix: [iamdflame/django/pulls](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pulls) ([#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/9)–[#21](https://github.com/iamdflame/django/pull/21); [fail→pass](evals/campaign_evidence.json)).
- **6 evidence issues, no code,** for the rest: 5 UNPROVEN (it could not prove either way) and 1 NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN: [#3](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/3) [#4](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/4) [#5](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/5) [#7](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/7) [#8](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/8) [#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/9).

## How it works

For one CVE and one maintained line (here: the fork's `stable/4.2.x-heirloom` branch), Heirloom runs
LOCATE → PROBE → CALIBRATE → PRESENCE → ADAPT → VERIFY → BEHAVIOUR → DECIDE → PUBLISH, every stage
recorded in a SQLite ledger so a killed run resumes without repeating side effects.

- **PROBE:** an independent porter model writes a regression test from the advisory and upstream's
  test diff; a leakage guard refuses prompts that contain the fix's added code.
- **CALIBRATE / PRESENCE:** the probe must FAIL on upstream's pre-fix commit (U⁻) and PASS on the fix
  (U⁺) with stable failing ids, run cleanly on the old line, and reach the code the fix touches
  (coverage). Only then does its result on the old line count; otherwise the verdict is UNPROVEN.
- **ADAPT / VERIFY:** headless Claude Code (in an Entire-tracked worktree) adapts the fix to the old
  line without touching `tests/`; VERIFY needs the probe FAIL→PASS and no new failures or skips in
  the touched test labels.
- **DECIDE:** real choices (behaviour differences, upstream test rewrites) open one question issue;
  the answer is stored as a precedent and reused.
- **PUBLISH:** a PR with one claim per fact, each linked to its neatlogs span and run artifact (a claim
  missing either is struck), or an evidence issue when there is no verified fix.

# Heirloom

**Heirloom is an agent that keeps end-of-life software patched.** For each new upstream security fix it writes an independent probe, calibrates it on upstream's own before/after commits, proves on the old line whether the bug is there, and then publishes either a verified candidate backport or the evidence of why it could not decide.

- **6 evidence issues, no code,** for the rest: 5 UNPROVEN (it could not prove either way) and 1 NOT_AFFECTED_PROVEN: [#3](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/3) [#4](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/4) [#5](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/5) [#7](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/7) [#8](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/8) [#9](https://github.com/iamdflame/heirloom/issues/9).

- These are **candidate backports, not Django releases**; nobody has reviewed or merged them.
- Tests run on **SQLite and PostGIS only**; backend-specific fixes (MySQL, Oracle, SpatiaLite) cannot be exercised.
- **UNPROVEN is by design** for what Heirloom cannot exercise: it publishes evidence, never a guess.
- The porter sees the advisory and upstream's test diff, **never the fix's code hunks**.
- The CVE-2026-87890 matrix probe is **hand-written** (the campaign's own 87890 probe came from the porter).

## How it works

For one CVE and one maintained line (here: the fork's `stable/4.2.x-heirloom` branch), Heirloom runs
LOCATE → PROBE → CALIBRATE → PRESENCE → ADAPT → VERIFY → BEHAVIOUR → DECIDE → PUBLISH, every stage
recorded in a SQLite ledger so a killed run resumes without repeating side effects.

- **PROBE:** an independent porter model writes a regression test from the advisory and upstream's
  test diff; a leakage guard refuses prompts that contain the fix's added code.
- **CALIBRATE / PRESENCE:** the probe must FAIL on upstream's pre-fix commit (U⁻) and PASS on the fix
  (U⁺) with stable failing ids, run cleanly on the old line, and reach the code the fix touches
  (coverage). Only then does its result on the old line count; otherwise the verdict is UNPROVEN.
- **ADAPT / VERIFY:** headless Claude Code (in an Entire-tracked worktree) adapts the fix to the old
  line without touching `tests/`; VERIFY needs the probe FAIL→PASS and no new failures or skips in
  the touched test labels.
- **DECIDE:** real choices (behaviour differences, upstream test rewrites) open one question issue;
  the answer is stored as a precedent and reused.
- **PUBLISH:** a PR with one claim per fact, each linked to its neatlogs span and run artifact (a claim
  missing either is struck), or an evidence issue when there is no verified fix.
